chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'The liar is the one who lies about something?' He said, 'No, there is no one except that this happens from him, but rather the one who is naturally inclined to lying.'

key_terms.الْكَذَّابُ: The liar / One who lies habitually

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between someone who lies occasionally and a true liar in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between occasional falsehood, which is universal, and the 'liar' who is stamped with the trait of habitual lying (al-matbu' 'ala al-kadhib). This distinction highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on *sima* (characteristic traits) over isolated actions, aligning with the concept of *fitrah* and the spiritual state of the heart. The hadith serves as a practical guide for self-assessment, urging believers to cultivate truthfulness as a permanent disposition rather than merely avoiding lies in specific instances.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The liar, he is the one who lies regarding something?’ There is no one except that would happen from him, but (it is the) one with the tendency for the lying’.
en.sarwar: 12. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Abd al- Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who has said the following: “Once I asked abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) ‘Is a liar one who lies about something?’
The Imam said, ‘No, there is no one who does not do so. It is those in whom lying becomes a thing of second nature.’”
